thread.title: Apple's self-driving vehicle meets first accident in California

author: Christina Harvey
title: Apple's self-driving vehicle meets first accident in California
text:
Apple's self-driving vehicle meets first accident in California September 02 By Christina Harvey
An Apple Inc (AAPL.O) self-driving auto was rear-ended while merging onto an expressway near the company's Silicon Valley headquarters this month, the company said in an accident report posted on Friday that confirmed the iPhone maker is still in the race to build autonomous vehicles.
The accident happened last week when the test vehicle, a Lexus SUV, was rear-ended by a 2016 Nissan Leaf, according to the filing on the DMV website. It was traveling at just 1 miles per hour and trying to merge into an expressway when a Nissan Leaf, going at 15 miles per hour, rear-ended it.
According to a California DMV report (PDF ), Apple's self-driving vehicle, in this case a modified Lexus RX 450h, had such an accident just last week.
According to BBC , Apple now has 66 such autonomous cars on the roads, with 111 drivers registered to operate them.
The self-driving cars, touted as the best bet for safe future travel, however, have been involved in some fatal accidents. He declined to respond to questions about whether the trailing vehicle could have been at fault.
The Apple auto carrying special equipment and sensors was hit by a Nissan vehicle from behind but neither car's passengers received any injuries.
Details about the incident surfaced in an autonomous vehicle collision report filed with the State of California Department of Motor Vehicles. Uber has said it plans to have self-driving cars back on the road by the end of the year.
